Summarize recorded fitting diagnostics

Source: R/diagnostics.R
diagnostics.Rd

Collect treatment-recoding information from atefit(), or recorded subgroup errors and warnings from count or survival catefit() and binary, count or survival catecv(), into a data frame. Each row represents one recorded message. Survival subgroup messages also remain in object[["errors/warnings"]].

Usage

diagnostics(
  object,
  type = c("messages", "propensity", "overlap"),
  layout = c("formatted", "arms", "metrics")
)

Arguments

object

A binary, count or survival atefit, a count or survival catefit, or a binary, count or survival catecv result.

type

Choose "messages" (the default) for recorded issues or "propensity" for full-sample treatment-model diagnostics from a binary, count or survival atefit result. "overlap" is an alias for "propensity".

layout

For overlap diagnostics, "formatted" (the default) returns a compact, rounded character table; "arms" returns one numeric row per treatment; "metrics" returns one numeric column per treatment and one row per diagnostic. Not used for messages.

Value

A data frame with columns method, split, iteration, group, subgroup, type, measure, and message. For count mutually exclusive groups, subgroup gives the lower and upper boundaries; survival uses the upper percentile label recorded by the estimator. For atefit, bootstrap failures have split bootstrap, the replicate number in iteration, and the affected estimate in measure. Split and iteration are NA for catefit. Otherwise, measure is NA unless the recorded message identifies it. Returns a zero-row data frame with the same columns when there are no recorded messages. For type = "propensity", the default formatted data frame has one row per diagnostic and one character column per treatment. Its percentages use the number of patients in the corresponding treatment group. Use layout = "arms" or layout = "metrics" for unrounded numeric results. The underlying diagnostics report sample size, untruncated propensity score range and median, number outside the other arm's observed score range, number truncated below and above the specified limits, and the median, maximum and effective sample size of the inverse treatment probability weights after truncation. The effective sample size is \((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\). These are treatment weights only, not censoring weights or the complete weights of a particular estimator. With layout = "formatted" or layout = "metrics", treatment columns use the original labels when available, or treatment 0 and treatment 1 otherwise. Older fitted objects do not contain this information.

Details

Overlap and weights describe the full analysis sample and the fitted treatment model; they do not establish covariate balance, positivity, or absence of unmeasured confounding. Extreme weights or little common support merit investigation, but no universal cutoff guarantees validity. The message view reports only diagnostics stored in the result, not every warning emitted during fitting. In particular, atefit() stores the treatment-recoding information and failed or undefined bootstrap estimates, but not all bootstrap warnings. Count fits record subgroup messages and support in object$subgroup.support. Continuous results are not supported by this helper.

Author

Thomas Debray tdebray@fromdatatowisdom.com

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
diagnostics(output_atefit)
diagnostics(output_atefit, type = "propensity")
diagnostics(output_atefit, type = "propensity", layout = "arms")
diagnostics(output_catecv)
subset(diagnostics(output_catecv), split == "validation")
} # }
